title: AMD raises $4.75bn in its biggest ever bond sale
excerpt: AMD has raised $4.75bn in its largest ever dollar bond sale, weeks after committing up to $5bn to Anthropic, a customer for its AI chips.
content_html:
AMD has raised $4.75bn in its biggest ever US dollar bond offering, sold in four tranches with maturities from three to ten years. It held $13.1bn in cash against $3.2bn of debt at the end of June, and has committed up to $5bn to Anthropic.

AMD has raised $4.75bn in the largest dollar bond sale it has ever done. The notes went out in four tranches with maturities from three to ten years, and demand was strong enough that the longest tranche priced about a quarter of a percentage point tighter than first indicated, at 0.9 points over Treasuries.

The company was not short of money. At the end of June it held $13.1bn in cash and short-term investments against $3.2bn of debt, which is an unusually clean balance sheet for a chipmaker at this scale.

What it has taken on is a commitment to a customer. In July AMD agreed to invest up to $5bn in Anthropic, alongside a partnership to deploy as much as two gigawatts of its Instinct MI450 chips to run Claude.

AMD has not connected the two. The filing says proceeds are for general corporate purposes, possibly including debt repayment, and the company has $875mn of bonds maturing next month.

The sizes are still hard to look past. The raise is $4.75bn and the Anthropic commitment is up to $5bn.

Either way it fits the shape the AI trade has taken, in which suppliers fund the customers who buy from them. Google has been running the same circular playbook with Anthropic, and Nvidia has gone further still, discussing guarantees over OpenAI’s data centre debt.

The underlying business is not imaginary. Analysts expect AMD revenue to climb 47% this year to more than $51bn, helped by the Anthropic agreement and a separate deal with Microsoft.

The borrowing is part of something much bigger. Big Tech’s AI debt has passed $350bn, and investment-grade issuers are now a routine part of that total rather than an exception.

Six banks ran the deal, among them JPMorgan, Citigroup and Bank of America. AMD last visited the investment-grade market in March 2025, when it raised $1.5bn, so this is more than three times that in 17 months.

A spokesperson said the company is “committed to maintaining its strong financial balance sheet,” which by any conventional measure it has. The interesting question is what a chipmaker holding $13bn in cash wants another $4.75bn for.

content_html_zh:
AMD 在其有史以来最大规模的美元债券发行中筹集了 47.5 亿美元，分四批发行，期限为 3 至 10 年。 截至 6 月底，该公司持有 131 亿美元现金，债务为 32 亿美元，并已向 Anthropic 承诺提供高达 50 亿美元的资金。

AMD 在其有史以来规模最大的美元债券发行中筹集了 47.5 亿美元。 这些票据分四批发行，期限从三年到十年不等，而且需求足够强劲，以至于最长的一批债券的定价比最初显示的要紧约四分之一个百分点，比国债高出0.9个百分点。

公司并不缺钱。 截至 6 月底，该公司持有 131 亿美元的现金和短期投资，而债务为 32 亿美元，对于如此规模的芯片制造商来说，这是一个异常干净的资产负债表。

它所承担的是对客户的承诺。 7 月，AMD 同意向 Anthropic 投资高达 50 亿美元，并与 Anthropic 合作部署多达 2 千兆瓦的 Instinct MI450 芯片来运行 Claude。

AMD尚未将两者联系起来。 文件称，所得款项用于一般公司用途，可能包括偿还债务，该公司还有 8.75 亿美元的债券将于下个月到期。

尺寸仍然很难看过去。 此次融资金额为 47.5 亿美元，Anthropic 承诺金额高达 50 亿美元。

无论哪种方式，它都符合人工智能行业的现状，即供应商为从他们那里购买产品的客户提供资金。 谷歌一直在与 Anthropic 运行同样的循环剧本，而 Nvidia 则走得更远，讨论对 OpenAI 数据中心债务的担保。

底层业务并不是想象中的。 分析师预计，得益于 Anthropic 协议以及与微软的单独交易，AMD 今年的收入将增长 47%，达到 510 亿美元以上。

借款是更大的事情的一部分。 大型科技公司的人工智能债务已超过 3500 亿美元，投资级发行人现在已成为这一债务总额的常规组成部分，而不是例外。

六家银行负责此次交易，其中包括摩根大通、花旗集团和美国银行。 AMD 上次登陆投资级市场是在 2025 年 3 月，当时筹集了 15 亿美元，因此这是 17 个月内融资额的三倍多。

一位发言人表示，该公司“致力于维持其强劲的财务资产负债表”，无论以任何传统衡量标准来看都是如此。 有趣的问题是，一家持有 130 亿美元现金的芯片制造商想要另外 47.5 亿美元做什么。
